summary: Added C++-compatible `-j/--jobs` handling and a worker budget to xs-rs: explicit `-jN` now splits a single large file into 4 MiB ranges on the sender and writes them concurrently on the receiver, while the default and `-j1` keep one-file I/O serial as the C++ does. The CLI now refuses unknown and explicitly unsupported options instead of ignoring them. All four gate commands pass, and the parent's `parallel_ranges_test.py` passes against the Rust binary.
diagnosis: The previous sender scanned and emitted DATA entirely on one thread and the receiver wrote every CHUNK inline in its frame loop; reading `src/remote.cpp:1560-1600` and `:2498-2510` showed the C++ only splits ranges when the raw `jobs` value is greater than one, and only unlocks concurrent per-file writes when that directory's `file_ranges` is true. The Rust HELLO writer also dropped the `jobs` INT_OPTIONS slot (index 5), so a C++ server never saw the client's budget. No timing regression was measured because the step is structural; correctness was measured by the parent range suite (26.25 s) and the cargo interop suite.
change: Added `rs/xs-rs/src/parallel.rs` with the default budget (4, clamped to MAX_WORKERS 64), explicit-range detection, parallel pread ranges, and a bounded-by-END write pool using pwrite. Threaded `jobs` through `Options`, the client HELLO and `options_from_flags`; `send_large`/`send_need_data` now split only when `-jN` (N>1) was explicit and at most one large file is in the NEED; the receiver stores completion context in `InFile` and publishes only after all queued writes finish. Rewrote relevant CLI parsing to add `-j`/`--jobs`, the C++ unsupported list, and unknown-option refusal, with `--help`/`--version`.
expected_effect: A single file of 32 MiB or more transfers with up to N overlapping reads and writes under explicit `-jN`, while default and `-j1` remain single-file serial, matching the C++ range semantics. `--jobs` now crosses HELLO so either side honours it, and a typo or unsupported rsync/xs option exits 1 before creating a destination.
risks: The write-pool queue is currently unbounded (like the pre-existing FrameOut queue), so a very fast sender into a slow disk can hold more than the C++ receiver's 16 MiB backlog. Options xs supports but xs-rs has not ported yet (filters, link-dest, files-from, chmod, info, size limits, install) are now refused as unsupported instead of silently ignored.
tests: Ran `XS_BIN=.../parent/build/xs cargo test --manifest-path rs/Cargo.toml`: all 17 binary unit tests, 5 compression, 5 hardlink, 9 interop, 5 io_control, 12 output, 8 ownership, 3 workers, 28 xs-wire unit, 4+4 xs-wire interop passed. Added CLI unit tests for `-j4`, `-aj4`, `-j 7`, `--jobs=2`, `--jobs 3`, default zero, refusal of unknown/unsupported options, and no-op acceptance; added HELLO byte-slot tests for jobs; added `rs/xs-rs/tests/workers.rs` covering all four C++/Rust directions with `-j4`, `-j1`/`-j0` large-file copies, and refusal before destination creation. Also ran `XSYNC_TEST_BINARY=.../rs/target/debug/xs-rs python3 tests/parallel_ranges_test.py` (OK, 5 tests, 1 skipped). Clippy `-D warnings`, fmt `--check`, and aarch64 `cargo check --all-targets` all pass.
commit_title: Port -j/--jobs worker ranges and refuse unknown options
commit_body: Wire jobs in INT_OPTIONS slot 5, default to four workers, and split one large file into 4 MiB ranges only when an explicit -jN (N > 1) asks for it, as fs.cpp:parallel_file_ranges and remote.cpp's Sender do. The receiver queues pwrite ranges and publishes each file only after END and every write completes; default and -j1 stay serial for one file. Unknown and explicitly unsupported options now fail before the destination is touched, matching main.cpp's parser.
